newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Vietnam soon to issue by-laws on mining - official.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam soon to issue by-laws on mining - official.

text.p: By-laws implementing Vietnam's recently-passed mining law will be enacted by the government very soon, said Do Hai Dung, deputy director-general of Vietnam's State Department of Management of Mineral Resources on Tuesday.

"The documents deal with taxation, land use, administrative sanctions, reporting procedure and state supervision and inspection," Do said in an address at the Asia Gold Congress currently being held in Hong Kong.
Vietnam's National Assembly passed a long-awaited Mineral Law on March 20, outlining terms and conditions related to prospecting, exploration, mining and processing minerals.
Do said that companies all over the world, including Australia, Canada, South Korea, New Zealand, Malaysia and Hong Kong, are awaiting licences for mineral exploration.
"Of the pending applications for exploration of solid minerals 85.7 percent are related to gold development," Do said in his speech.
Of the already-granted mineral titles 56.6 percent are related to gold development, Do said.

"At this very moment the Vietnam Gem and Gold Corporation (VIGEGO) is working out a master plan for gold development projects and to carry our exploration work on the areas promising for gold mineralization," he said.
Vietnam has 45 gold deposits and occurrences under exploitation so far, Do said, but noted that the gold mining industry was plagued by artisanal, semi-mechanized production methods.
"Some areas are seriously polluted and land is damaged due to illegal mining by local people," Do said.
About 57 percent of Vietnam's gold reserves is quartz sulphide gold, widely distributed over the country, Do said, adding that Bong Mieu and Paclang were typical examples.

Vietnam granted three joint venture Foreign Investment Licences between 1991 and 1994, Do said, listing the Bong Mieu Gold Mine in Quang Nam - Da Nang Province, the Nari joint venture in Bac Thai Province and the Ban Cong joint venture in Thanh Hoa Province.
